summary: Drives co-change derivation against real throwaway git repos rather than a mocked git log. Its git()/commit() helpers take the repo directory EXPLICITLY: they used to read a module-level `repo` that each scratch-repo test swapped and restored in a finally, and when the ~90-commit partner-cap test overran vitest's 5s default under full-suite load, vitest moved on while that swap was still in place — so later tests silently ran against the wrong repo and failed intermittently (partners['a.py'] undefined). That test now carries an explicit 60s timeout.

summary: Covers deriveCoChange (the git walk) and the gs rendering of the Moves together section. Two things a future editor needs: the helpers `git`/`commit` take the repo dir as an explicit parameter and must keep doing so — they once read a module-level `repo` that each scratch-repo test swapped and restored, and when the ~90-commit partner-cap test overran vitest's 5s default under full-suite load vitest moved on while the swap was live, so later tests silently ran against the wrong repo and the suite failed only under load. That test now carries an explicit 60s timeout for the same reason. The rendering block asserts co-change appears in EVERY gs view and that import-graph neighbours stay excluded even in a view that lists neither imports nor importers.
